summary: Compared per-project extension configs across workspaces and found that switching threads correctly reflects each project's resolved extensions. Identified a real bug: per-project overrides cannot turn a Pi extension on if it is globally disabled — `ProjectIntegrationResolver.resolve` gates on the global `enabled` flag before the override, and `enabledPiExtensionPaths` filters on the same global flag, so e.g. cronkis's `unity: true` / `svelte: true` overrides are ignored.
decisions: Treat the original 'switching threads shows wrong extensions' theory as not reproduced — sidebar clicks, workspace Overview → Threads, page reload, new thread in another workspace, and command palette all show correct per-project extensions.

Attribute the observed inconsistency to per-project overrides being unable to enable a globally-disabled Pi extension, not to switching. Fixing it would require loading a globally-disabled Pi extension when a project opts in, changing extension-loading semantics — flagged as needing user sign-off before changing.

Abandon the test-data cleanup attempt: deleting threads raced with something recreating them, the delete-confirmation dialog kept intercepting clicks, and 4 empty 'New thread' threads remain across mchan (×2), jev-melee (×1), and cronkis (×1).
errors: Earlier comparison truncated output to 500 chars and only compared identical alphabetical prefixes, masking real per-project differences.

Cleanup Playwright scripts `/tmp/cleanup2.mjs` and `/tmp/cleanup5.mjs` failed with a 30s TimeoutError because `<div id="bits-c27" data-dialog-overlay>` intercepts pointer events on the New thread button, preventing the delete-confirmation flow from completing.
